primary_source_citation.title: USGS Ecosystems Mission Area Technical Reference: Ecosystem Trophic Pyramid & Lindeman 10 Percent Energy Law

1.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Only 10 percent of energy transfers up each trophic level; 90 percent dissipates as metabolic heat and life processes.
core_mechanism_bullets: Level 4: Apex Predators (1 kcal): Red-tailed hawks, ospreys, and wolves depend on thousands of acres of intact lower-level habitat.
Level 3: Secondary Consumers (10 kcal): Brook trout, frogs, insectivorous songbirds, and red foxes regulate herbivore populations.
Level 2: Primary Consumers (100 kcal): Native honeybees, caterpillars, deer, and aquatic macroinvertebrates convert plant tissue into biomass.
Level 1: Producers & Decomposers (1,000 kcal): Trees, native grasses, and algae fix solar energy via photosynthesis while fungi recycle dead organic matter.
1.worked_field_example: Step 1: Read the official Environmental Science Requirement 1 prompt carefully and underline every action verb. Step 2: Apply the field rule of thumb (Only 10 percent of energy transfers up each trophic level; 90 percent dissipates as metabolic heat and life processes.). Step 3: Verify each measurement or checkpoint against USGS Ecosystems Mission Area reference criteria and record your findings in your Scout Workbook.
1.counselor_tabletop_demo: 3-Minute Troop Tabletop Demo (Req 1): Display environmental_science_trophic_10pct_v46_diagram.png on screen, divide Scouts into buddy pairs for a 90-second hands-on walkthrough of 'Ecosystem Trophic Pyramid & Lindeman 10 Percent Energy Law', and have each pair state the key threshold (Only 10 percent of energy transfers up each trophic level; 90 percent dissipates as metabolic heat and life processes.) in their own words before sign-off.
1.real_world_connection_box: USGS Ecosystems Mission Area Field Standard: Only 10 percent of energy transfers up each trophic level; 90 percent dissipates as metabolic heat and life processes.
1.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + USGS Ecosystems Mission Area

2.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: About 25 fine PM2.5 particles fit across the width of one single human hair (60 microns), letting them reach deep lung alveoli.
core_mechanism_bullets: PM2.5 Fine Combustion Aerosol (<2.5 um): Emitted by wildfire smoke, tailpipes, and power plants; penetrates deep into lung alveoli and bloodstream.
PM10 Inhalable Coarse Dust (<10 um): Pollen, unpaved road dust, and mold spores trapped mostly in upper nasal passages and bronchi.
Human Hair Reference Diameter (60 um): Visible benchmark used in Scout Vaseline index-card particulate collection experiments (Req 3a).
Clean Air Act (1970 / 1990) Impact: Cut 6 common U.S. criteria air pollutants by over 78 percent while U.S. GDP more than tripled.

primary_source_citation.title: U.S. EPA Watershed Academy & USGS Technical Reference: Watershed Hydrology: Point vs. Non-Point Pollution & Riparian Buffers

3.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Never pour motor oil or paint down storm drains; storm grates flow untreated straight into local creeks and rivers.
core_mechanism_bullets: Point-Source Discharge (NPDES Permit): Discrete factory or wastewater treatment pipe regulated directly under the 1972 Clean Water Act.
Non-Point Stormwater Runoff: Diffuse lawn fertilizer, pet waste, road salt, and brake dust washed across pavement into streams.
Eutrophication & Algal Blooms: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus trigger dense algae growth that depletes dissolved oxygen for fish.
Riparian Buffer & Rain Garden Filter: 100-foot native root zones slow stormwater velocity, trap eroded silt, and absorb excess nutrients.

primary_source_citation.title: USDA NRCS & U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Technical Reference: Honeybee Pollination Mechanics, Colony Health & Erosion Control

4.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Insect pollinators are essential to more than 1 in every 3 bites of food (over 90 commercial U.S. fruit, nut, and vegetable crops).
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. Floral Nectar & Pollen Transfer: Branched electrostatic body hairs trap pollen grains and cross-pollinate blossoms across a 2-mile foraging radius.
2. Waggle Dance Vector Navigation: Worker bees encode exact solar angle and distance to rich wildflower patches on vertical honeycomb.
3. Four Stressors on Pollinators: Varroa destructor mites, habitat fragmentation, neonicotinoid misuse, and floral monocultures.
4. Scout Habitat & Erosion Action: Plant continuous-bloom native wildflowers and use mulch, silt fences, and terraced slopes to stop topsoil loss.
